Ubiquitous drone use by both sides, sometime connected by hair-thin fiber optic cables to defeat electronic jamming, have transformed the battlefield since Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

articles.title: How does Iran view shift in US approach after JD Vance ordered away?
articles.summary: Washington believes maritime blockade, overland border disruptions, air restrictions and isolating sanctions are working
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Decision-makers in Iran are now considering the implications of Vice President JD Vance’s removal from the Iran file to focus on domestic issues, which analysts say could increase the chances of conflict between the two sides.

Vance has been the US’s chief negotiator in talks with Iran, but US President Donald Trump told him to direct his focus on alleged Democratic “corruption”, according to a post by Trump on Truth Social on Thursday. He added that a deal with Iran was no longer a priority for the government.

The vice president is believed to be viewed by Tehran as one of the more pragmatic figures in the Trump administration since the US and Israel launched their surprise war on Iran on February 28.

Nasser Hadian, professor of international relations at the University of Tehran, said that by assigning Vance to the case of alleged domestic corruption, Trump was mainly signalling a confrontation with the Democrats after their sweeping victories against the governing Republican Party in the midterm elections.

But the move may also serve Israel, which is reportedly eager for Trump to launch new strikes against Iran , after Vance blamed the Republicans’ humiliating defeat in the midterms on the war .

“Another signal is to Iran, essentially saying reaching a deal now is not a priority, and that the person known to have a relatively softer stance on Iran was redirected to other issues,” Hadian said.

Vance is believed to have been in favour of a negotiated resolution to the war, due to its rising economic costs for US citizens and their opposition to the war suggested in opinion polls.

The vice president was backed by Trump envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff when he negotiated the now-defunct memorandum of understanding with Iran in June, which briefly paused the war and resumed shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Rubio has, meanwhile, called Iranian authorities “insane” for their demands on ending the war. But he also acknowledged the cost of an all-out war and seeks to win via deepening economic pressure and isolation on all Iranians.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who has faced an impeachment vote due to his role in the war , and Central Command chief Brad Cooper are reportedly in favour of renewed military action against Iran .

Vance wrote a letter to Iran’s security chief , Mohsen Rezaei, in late October, as regional mediators redoubled their efforts to bridge gaps between the two sides. Rezaei initially described the tone of the missive as positive, but by last week, he was addressing claims of progress and a possible direct meeting with Vance as “fake news about imaginary talks”.

“You lost the war and the election. Vance has conceded, Rubio is heading for the exit, Hegseth is about to be fired, and the CENTCOM commander is now a podcaster!” he wrote on X at the time.

Mediated contacts are ongoing between the two sides, but no breakthrough is expected. Tehran is demanding seven conditions and clear sequencing of concessions to end the war, but this is appearing to be unacceptable to the US.

Mohammad Saleh Sedghian, director of the Arab Center for Iranian Studies, pointed out that Trump has repeatedly highlighted alleged rifts within the Iranian negotiating team. But he said Iranian authorities were also questioning the reliability of another potential agreement with Washington.

“Even if you can imagine Mr Rezaei sitting down with Mr Vance, and reaching a deal? What guarantee is there that Trump will enforce it?” he told Al Jazeera.

The atmosphere of mistrust between the two sides is also complicating prospects of a deal, he added. This means that the ongoing US siege on Iran and harsh sanctions will continue, something that could cost Iran more than a relatively shorter military conflict with Washington, he added.

“The blockade and disruptions are significantly raising the costs for Iranian people. The current state of no war and no negotiated resolution is very dangerous,” Sedghian said.

Iranian reformist newspaper Shargh argued this week that Vance’s role concerning Iran is unresolved rather than definitely terminated, but also said the conflict could further escalate.

Conservative Farhikhtegan daily disputed the portrayal of Vance as genuinely antiwar, arguing that diplomacy, military force and economic pressure ultimately serve a common objective for the US in trying to coerce Iran to accept its conditions.

For now, the two sides are continuing to fight over control in the Strait of Hormuz, with retaliatory attacks on shipping and military installations.

On Friday and Saturday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and regular army separately claimed several new incidents of vessels either hitting naval mines or being struck by projectiles after attempting “unauthorised” routes in the critical waterway.

The latest weekly report by the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) on Friday reported eight incidents in and around the strait, mostly in the southern route near Oman.

UKMTO also recorded 139 outbound and 169 inbound transits through the strait during the week, approximately 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.

Hadian believes that Iranian decision-makers will not tolerate the current situation indefinitely.

“The authorities will either go after their warships, their vessels, or their military bases,” he added. “The stronger the blockade becomes, including through maritime pressure and disruptions for overland borders and air travel, war becomes more probable.”

But Trump’s sidelining of Vance on the Iran issue will not radically alter the current situation, Hadian said, since Washington believes its tactic of economic pressure on Tehran can force it to make concessions.

“The US would have done this with or without Vance, and I believe it will continue to do this,” he said.

articles.title: A Mississippi man said his brother destroyed a newer will before dying, which would leave him the entire estate; a November 10 appeals court upheld the signed 2003 will instead, leaving most of the estate to cousins
articles.summary: A dispute over a Mississippi man’s estate has ended with the Court of Appeals upholding a will signed more than two decades earlier.
articles.body: A dispute over a Mississippi man’s estate has ended with the Court of Appeals upholding a will signed more than two decades earlier. The case, In the Matter of the Estate of Lamar DeLoach, decided on 10 November 2026, turned on whether a later document had validly revoked the 2003 will, and whether the brother who claimed the estate had enough evidence to prove his version of events, as per the report on Justia U.S. Law.Lamar DeLoach signed a last will and testament on 18 July 2003 and died on 23 January 2023. His cousins, Larry and Rodney DeLoach, filed to probate that will shortly after his death, while his brother, Frank DeLoach, argued that Lamar had later made and then destroyed a newer will. Read more details about it, as per the court report, here:The 2003 will and its termsThe 2003 will was prepared by attorney Phil Embry, who signed the document as a witness along with his secretary, Teena Newton. It named Larry and Rodney as co-executors and left $100,000 to Garner Jo Myers.The remainder of Lamar’s property was left to Larry and Rodney, his cousins. That arrangement became the foundation of the estate plan that the court ultimately upheld.On 28 February 2023, Larry and Rodney filed a petition to probate the 2003 will. The chancery court admitted it to probate on 13 March 2023 and appointed the two cousins as co-executors of the estate.Frank’s claim about a later willFrank DeLoach argued that Lamar had executed a later will in 2012 that expressly revoked the 2003 document. He claimed that Lamar later destroyed the 2012 will, which would mean Lamar died without a valid will.If that argument had succeeded, Frank said the entire estate would have passed to him as Lamar’s sole heir. That would have displaced the cousins and the $100,000 gift to Garner Jo Myers.Frank filed a will contest and a motion for injunctive relief on 1 June 2023. He argued that the 2012 instrument had revoked the 2003 will and that its later destruction left the estate to be divided under intestacy rules.What the witnesses saidFrank relied on statements from Audrea and Joe to support his account. Joe said he advised Lamar to burn the 2012 will so it could not be pieced back together.Joe assumed that Lamar had burned the document after their discussion, but he did not actually witness the destruction. That gap became important, because the court needed proof that the later will had been validly executed in the first place.The chancellor found that the affidavits from Audrea and Joe did not meet the legal standard required under Mississippi law. Without that proof, the claim that the 2012 will had ever been validly made could not stand.Why the later will failedThe central problem was that Frank could not produce a validly executed 2012 will. The only document that met the requirements of Mississippi Code Annotated section 91-5-3 was the 2003 will itself.The court explained that if a later will containing a revocation clause was not validly made and executed, that revocation clause has no effect. In such a case, the earlier will remains the governing document.The chancellor granted summary judgment in favour of Larry and Rodney on 22 March 2024. He ruled that Frank had failed to show that the 2012 instrument was legally viable, which made the question of whether it revoked the 2003 will moot.The appeals court’s decisionFrank appealed, arguing that the chancellor had erred in granting summary judgment and that the ruling was wrong on the facts. The Court of Appeals reviewed the case and found no error.The court agreed that Frank had failed to produce a valid subsequent will that revoked the 2003 document. It also agreed that the issue of whether the 2012 will was later destroyed was irrelevant, since the document had never been properly executed in the first place.The Court of Appeals affirmed the chancery court’s decision in full. The 2003 will remains the last valid will and testament of Lamar DeLoach.What this means for the estateThe practical effect is that the estate will be distributed according to the 2003 will. Larry and Rodney, as co-executors, will carry out the terms of that document.Garner Jo Myers will receive the $100,000 gift, and the remainder of the property will go to the cousins. Frank’s claim that he should inherit the entire estate has been rejected.The case highlights the need to follow the proper legal process when making or revoking a will. A document that is not properly executed cannot be used to change an earlier valid will, even if there are claims that it was later destroyed.An lesson in estate planningThe case is a reminder to families dealing with estates that verbal assurances, and informal agreements, don’t cut it. Wills must meet specific legal requirements to be valid, and those requirements do not disappear simply because someone says a document was burned.The ruling of the Court of Appeals makes it clear that the burden of proof is on the party challenging an existing will. Without solid evidence that a later will was properly made, the earlier document controls.For Frank DeLoach, the outcome means the estate will not pass to him as Lamar’s sole heir. For Larry and Rodney, it confirms their role as executors and beneficiaries under the 2003 will.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: U.S. floated idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: U.S. negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine’s potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, following the latest round of peace ⁠talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi.
articles.body: U.S. negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine’s potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, following the latest round of peace ⁠talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi. This is the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised during the talks, Zelenskyy said in remarks to reporters released by his office on Saturday. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?” he said. “That is why I believe NATO is back on the agenda. But you have also heard (Russian President Vladimir) Putin’s signals, and this is an extremely difficult ⁠conversation.” Putin has long said Ukrainian membership of NATO is a red line ​for ⁠Moscow, citing the issue as one reason for launching Russia’s full-blown invasion in 2022. Zelenskyy reiterated his position that Kyiv was not ready to concede territory but said that if it received a comprehensive package including security guarantees, the right ⁠to a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a national referendum. Echoing comments made by European leaders at ‌a summit in Dublin on Friday, Zelenskyy dismissed Russia’s call for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before the specifics are agreed on how to end the war in Ukraine. “We cannot turn everything upside down and start by talking about changing ‌the security framework in the world or across the continent overall, and only ‌then talk about ending this war. This war must be ended first,” he said. Zelenskyy also dismissed Putin’s suggestion for a local humanitarian ceasefire in Kostiantynivka, a hotly contested city in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region, saying it reflected Moscow’s inability to take the city by force. Civilians there have already had the opportunity to evacuate, he added. “Putin simply ⁠wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city that way,” he said. Ukraine has given a list of seven or eight other frontline settlements where civilians, including children, are trapped for a potential humanitarian truce but Russia prefers to use them as military targets, Zelenskyy said. Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians in the war. Large prisoner exchange agreed The two days of U.S.-brokered talks between Ukraine and Russia concluded on Wednesday in the Emirati capital without a major breakthrough, though the sides agreed to a prisoner exchange that will involve more than 1,000 people, Zelenskyy said. The final numbers for the prisoner swap were still under discussion, he added. U.S. ‌peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had pledged to raise an energy ceasefire with Putin at a ​meeting in Moscow on Thursday, Zelenskyy said, but there was no news of any progress after their talks. “Putin personally does ‌not support a ceasefire,” he said. Zelenskyy met Witkoff and ⁠Kushner on Thursday in Ireland after their talks in Moscow. He said the US negotiators had told him that all ⁠sides had agreed for Europe to have a seat at the negotiating table in forthcoming peace talks. In Abu Dhabi, delegates from Europe — which is now Ukraine’s largest financial ‌and military backer — had talks with US ​and Ukrainian officials but did not sit at the table with ‌Russia. At the summit in Ireland, E.U. leaders agreed that ​Europe’s team for any Ukraine peace talks would comprise five major military powers — non-E.U. member Britain plus France, Germany, Italy and Poland — as well as E.U. officials.

articles.title: Young musicians connect a community across the Line of Control
articles.summary: Sharing Shina songs online, musicians in Kashmir, Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan renew ties across the divide.
articles.body:
This feature is part of a series examining how artificial borders reshape daily life, divide families and force loved ones to navigate the human cost of political geography.

In the remote Tulail Valley close to the Line of Control in Indian-administered Kashmir, 25-year-old singer Aasim Yaseen was walking through his village, Buglinder, when a college student from a neighbouring hamlet stopped him.

The young man, Tanveer, took out his phone and played Sangh Mukh Shamah, a song Yaseen had recently released in Shina, their shared language.

“People here don’t consider music work,” he says.

“Sometimes I think about going into another profession, but then someone plays my song on their phone, and I keep going.”

Across Gurez in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, Drass in Indian-administered Ladakh, and Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan, young musicians like Yaseen are sharing Shina songs on social media. They are helping keep their language alive and renewing ties within a community that has been divided for generations.

The songs cross the Line of Control, which divides Indian- and Pakistani-administered parts of Kashmir. But the musicians face financial pressures, unreliable internet connections and political restrictions on their movement.

articles.title: Endangered salmon leap back after Lake District bends restored
articles.summary: The rewiggling was aimed at restoring Atlantic salmon's habitat, and reducing flood risk.
articles.body:
An endangered breed of salmon is making a recovery after a stream in the Lake District was rewiggled.

Swindale Beck was straightened in the 1800s to increase land for farming, but the quicker-moving water scoured away the gravel banks needed by Atlantic salmon to lay their eggs.

A decade after the restoration project between the RSPB and United Utilities, an Environment Agency survey found fry - newly hatched salmon - at three locations showed numbers had more than doubled in the past two years.

A spokesman described the results as "encouraging" and showed the habitat was now providing environment to boost numbers of one of the UK's most threatened fish species.

As well as the restoration of a 1km (0.6 mile) section of river to a more natural wiggly course, further work downstream allowed other sections to reconnect with their floodplain, reducing flood risk and also create a wider range of places for wildlife to thrive.

Along with salmon, the survey found brown trout, lamprey and eels.

And the restored wetland habitat had become home to a host of plants and wildlife including snipe, kingfishers and goosander.

Fisheries technical specialist Philip Ramsden, from the Environment Agency in Cumbria, said: "In this year's surveys, we found significantly more salmon fry across the three sites we sample on one section of Swindale Beck, along with a good sprinkling of parr [juvenile salmon].

"This indicates that young salmon are now not simply moving into this habitat from upstream or downstream, but have come from redds [salmon nests] that adult salmon have been able to create in this section, as it is now providing the gravels and other conditions that they need."

Ramsden said it was "really encouraging" to see.

"I'm sure that this is the start of a real acceleration of establishment as a stronghold of spawning and juvenile habitat for these fish," he said.

"As expected, it's taken a few years, but results this year are really pleasing to see."

articles.title: Pentagon's former UFO investigator offers simple theory for mysterious jellyfish-shaped object on video
articles.summary: Video near Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson captures a jellyfish-shaped object with dangling strands, but a former Pentagon UFO investigator suggests kite.
articles.body: A bizarre, jellyfish-shaped object filmed moving through the sky near a major U.S. military base in Anchorage, Alaska, has sparked online speculation, but the Pentagon's former top UFO investigator says there may be a much simpler explanation. Video recorded June 15 shows a dark object appearing to hover along a mountainside near a rainbow, with several long strands dangling beneath it. The object appears to pulse and shift in the air as the strands rise, fall and wave beneath it. As it moves toward the left side of the frame, the strands trail behind before the object moves back toward the right. NEW PENTAGON UFO FILES DETAIL FBI AGENTS' SIGHTING OF SILENT TRIANGULAR OBJECT WITH NO VISIBLE ENGINES Sara Jane Osborn recorded the unusual sighting and posted the video to Facebook the following day. "It looks like a friggin alien. I don't like it," Osborn can be heard saying as she records the object. "It's moving very weirdly," she says moments later. Fox News Digital reached out to Osborn for additional details about the sighting. Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson confirmed to Fox News Digital that officials are aware of the footage. "We are aware of a video circulating on social media regarding a reported aerial sighting near Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson from June 15, 2026, but have no additional information to provide at this time," the base's 673d Air Base Wing Public Affairs office said in a statement. NEW TRUMP UFO FILE DUMP INCLUDES MILITARY FOOTAGE OF MYSTERIOUS STAR-SHAPED OBJECT Sean Kirkpatrick, who led the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), which investigates unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAP, cautioned against relying on social media footage to assess unexplained sightings. "I don't usually make any assessment from an online video," Kirkpatrick told Fox News Digital. "First, as I've said many times, social media is not a good source of data for anything, let alone UAP sightings." NASA CHIEF CONFIRMS AGENCY HAS UNEXPLAINED UFO IMAGERY: 'WE DON'T KNOW WHAT IT IS' "The video, if authentic and not generated, is compressed and cannot be used for data analysis. It's too easy to make up video now and cover your signatures," he added. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Kirkpatrick said the footage alone does not provide enough information to determine the object's size, altitude, distance or actual movement. He did, however, point to a possible explanation for what appears in the video. "The motion is similar to a kite with streamers, particularly the waves," Kirkpatrick said. articles.title: 'Exposes BJP's tall claims that everything is hunky-dory': Congress on recent J&K attacks
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir Congress chief Tariq Karra on Saturday said recent attacks in the Valley had exposed the Centre's \"tall claims of peace\" and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir Congress chief Tariq Karra on Saturday said recent attacks in the Valley had exposed the Centre's "tall claims of peace" and that "everything is hunky-dory" in the Union Territory.Speaking to reporters at a party function marking the birth anniversary of India’s first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, Karra cited the attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam and the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar as evidence that the security situation remained a concern.He criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for citing open markets, functioning schools and the absence of strikes or stone-pelting as signs of normalcy in Kashmir, alleging that such claims overlooked the situation on the ground."Whenever something like this happens, the government of India stands in the dock. You must have heard repeatedly, both inside and outside Parliament, whether it is the prime minister or the home minister; when it suits them, they say Kashmir is very peaceful, and nothing happens there," he said.Karra alleged that the Centre tried to project an image of peace internationally but was exposed by its "poor performance and wrong policies"."Such incidents expose the tall claims of the BJP, including those of the prime minister and home minister, that everything is hunky-dory... It (attacks) is a failure of the security apparatus and the policies adopted by the government of India," he said."The Centre forgets that this is a deceptive calm. If this is not a deceptive calm, then how do such incidents happen?" he added.Karra’s remarks came days after terrorists riding a motorcycle opened fire on CRPF personnel at a checkpoint in Kulgam district on Wednesday afternoon, injuring three security personnel.The attack took place around 2.15 pm, when the assailants fired at the personnel before fleeing, officials said. The injured were taken to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment.In a separate incident in Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of two SPOs who had gone missing on Wednesday were recovered on Thursday morning. The two personnel went missing while travelling from their camp towards an Army post at Dharna-Marwah on Wednesday.When asked about actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut’s remarks on Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s book, Karra said he did not take Ranaut seriously. He said the comments reflected a lack of political maturity, culture and values.He added that the remarks would neither diminish Gandhi’s stature and respect nor weaken her resolve to revive democracy in the country. "The BJP and its mindset is getting exposed, that's all," he said.Paying tribute to Nehru, Karra described him as one of the senior-most leaders of modern India, saying he had made great sacrifices for the country’s independence.He said Nehru laid the foundation of modern India, a legacy later carried forward by Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi and other Congress leaders. Karra said Indian democracy was once admired and followed by countries around the world, but alleged that the BJP had weakened the democratic system.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said authorities had found no evidence of a cyberattack. articles.title: Noel Fielding 'appalled' by jokes he made with Russell Brand
articles.summary: The Great British Bake Off presenter says he has not been in contact with the convicted rapist "for many years".
articles.body:
Noel Fielding has said he is "appalled" by jokes he made alongside Russell Brand when the pair appeared together on TV and at live shows.

The Great British Bake Off presenter said in a statement to the Sun he was "horrified and deeply disturbed" to learn of Brand's crimes, after the disgraced comedian was jailed for rape and sexual assault.

Footage of Fielding and Brand joking about rape with TV presenter Jonathan Ross on an episode of Channel 4's Big Fat Quiz of the Year in 2007 has resurfaced in the aftermath of Brand's conviction.

Fielding described "some of the jokes" he made as "horrible and inappropriate", and said he had not been in contact with Brand "for many years".

"I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand's crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice," Fielding said.

"I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. I have had no contact with him for many years.

"Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them."

The BBC has contacted Fielding for comment.

Ross has also released a statement distancing himself from the remarks, saying that his "thoughts are with the many, many women who have bravely come forward."

Among the resurfaced footage is a clip of Brand and Fielding laughing on an episode of The Russell Brand Show, which aired on BBC Radio 2 in 2007. In it, Brand joked about kissing and holding an underage grasshopper.

"How do you even know if it's a child or an adult? You don't even care, do you," Fielding responded.

Brand can be heard replying: "It's a mistake I've made. I've had a lot of problems in the past, because I thought a grasshopper was above age. Before I know it, I'm in it, right, I'm kissing it, I'm holding it. Then it turns around and looks at me with onyx eyes and says: 'I'm 12.'"

Brand and Fielding also performed charity gigs together as The Goth Detectives.

Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others.

Further allegations against him have been made in recent days. More women have made allegations about him in interviews with the Times and a Netflix documentary.

The Times said it could not publish the investigation until the criminal case ended. Brand has denied non-consensual sexual activity.

Police have said Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women.

The disgraced entertainer is being detained at HMP Wandsworth. BBC News has asked his legal representatives for a response to the latest allegations.

If you are affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

articles.title: Comedians call out Dave Chappelle over 'disgusting' routine celebrating Charlie Kirk's murder
articles.summary: Comedians including Rob Schneider and Tim Young condemned Dave Chappelle after leaked video showed him saying he feels better following Charlie Kirk's assassination.
articles.body: Comedians Rob Schneider and Tim Young are criticizing Dave Chappelle after the veteran comic said during a New York stand-up set that he "feels better" following the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. The backlash follows video circulating online of Chappelle’s performance at Madison Square Garden, where he made remarks about Kirk's murder. "I feel f---ed up saying this. It’s scary being a public speaker. And I mean, look, ever since that guy, Charlie Kirk, got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but, I feel better," Chappelle could be heard saying in the clip. "I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling. I didn’t ask to feel this way," Chappelle said. "I just be driving around like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood? Oh!'" Chappelle continued on Friday. CHARLAMAGNE THA GOD CALLS OUT DAVE CHAPPELLE'S KIRK COMMENTS, WOULDN'T WISH THEM 'ON MY WORST ENEMY' On Nov 9, actor and comedian Rob Schneider wrote an open letter to Chappelle on X, accusing the comic of abandoning the compassion and openness that once defined his comedy. "You are not the same human being you once were," Schneider said. "You are no longer a champion of compassionate freedom of thought, a person who makes people question their prejudices and preconceived judgements. An entertainer who asks their audience to open their minds and hearts more." He added that Chappelle was now a "champion of senseless violence" and wrote, "Nobody deserves to die for engaging in conversation. And no one should ‘feel better’ after the violent murder of a husband, a father, a son and a friend." Schneider concluded by saying he still considered Chappelle a friend and expressed hope that he would rediscover what Schneider described as the "spirit of generosity and compassion that earned you the love and respect of so many of us." TURNING POINT USA SPOX ANDREW KOLVET SPEAKS OUT AS JENNIFER WELCH, DAVE CHAPPELLE MOCK CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER Comedian and political commentator Tim Young also called Chappelle's remarks "disgusting," pointing to Kirk's previous defense of Chappelle after an attacker assaulted the comedian onstage at the Hollywood Bowl in 2022. "It's actually extra disappointing to me that when Dave Chappelle was attacked on stage, Charlie Kirk was one of the first people and probably the biggest person on the right to defend Dave Chappelle and say that there shouldn't be any violence for speech," Young told Fox News Digital. "It's such a disappointing statement from Dave Chappelle now." Young speculated that Chappelle's comments could be an effort to regain favor with the political left after years of criticism over his comedy about transgender issues. "This might be an attempt by him to get back in the good graces of the left," Young said. "I think him making fun of Charlie Kirk's murder is, again, you're performing for this other side that you may have lost a little bit of your audience from. But at this point, Dave Chappelle is so successful and so rich, he doesn't need to perform for anybody to get there." CHAPPELLE, JENNIFER WELCH JOKES ABOUT KIRK'S MURDER PART OF PATTERN OF LEFTISTS FINDING HUMOR IN VIOLENCE Young also argued that comedians have become comfortable joking about violence against conservatives because they operate within politically like-minded entertainment circles. "Mainstream comedy is very comfortable making fun of Charlie Kirk's murder because they live in a bubble," Young said. "When you get into the Hollywood bubble, when you get into the SNL bubble, you're around a bunch of liberals who agree with you. And if people disagree with you, they'll be canceled." Fox News Digital reached out to a representative for Chappelle for comment. Chappelle is not the only comedian to incorporate Kirk's death into his material. Former "Saturday Night Live" star Pete Davidson and current cast member Michael Che have also made jokes referencing the conservative activist's killing. "Tony reminds me of Charlie Kirk in that he’s definitely been on camera letting a guy unload in his throat," Davidson said during Netflix’s "The Roast of Kevin Hart" in May, referring to fellow comedian Tony Hinchcliffe. LIBERAL PODCASTERS APOLOGIZE AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT DIGGING UP CHARLIE KIRK'S BODY Che also referenced Kirk in his Netflix special, "Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota," which premiered Oct. 13. "I feel like Erika Kirk on this stage. That’s no disrespect to the Kirks, by the way," Che said. The comedian said that he didn’t know who Charlie Kirk was before his death. Che joked that he initially thought people were talking about "the dude from Star Trek." Kirk was murdered during an appearance at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025. His widow, Erika Kirk, has condemned jokes about political assassination, warning that such rhetoric reflects a broader cultural problem. "A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay," she wrote on X. "It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard. Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates," she added.
